clue.text: Cut down new academic work, something added in text

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut down
a thesis is a long piece of academic writing

explanation.surface: Someone trims a fresh dissertation and slips an aside into the text.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracketed aside inserted into a sentence is exactly this kind of interpolation.

clue.text: Baker's work, supposedly a piece of cake

definitions.meaning: a baked pastry dish a baker produces
the idiom easy as this pastry dish means very easy

explanation.surface: Something a baker made, said to be as easy as anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker makes these pastry dishes, and the phrase easy as one means something simple.

clue.text: Characters for this include Romeo and Juliet

definitions.text: Characters for this include Romeo and Juliet

parts.words: Characters for this include Romeo and Juliet
parts.note: Romeo and Juliet are code words for R and J in the phonetic alphabet used in wireless communication

explanation.surface: A drama whose cast list features Shakespeare's star-crossed lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like a play's cast, but means letters, spelled out in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phonetic alphabet of Alpha, Bravo and so on was devised for clear spoken transmission over the airwaves.

clue.text: Common sense about prince in Tower being edgy

indicators.note: about says the common-sense word goes around the prince

parts.note: nous is British informal for common sense
Edward V, one of the Princes in the Tower, as a royal cipher E R V (Edward Rex the fifth)

explanation.surface: A sensible person grows anxious about a prince locked in the Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Princes in the Tower were the boy king Edward V and his brother, held in the Tower of London in 1483; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling edgy means being anxious and on tenterhooks.

clue.text: Taking on about broken end creating obstacle

indicators.note: about says the employing word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: taking on staff is hiring them

indicators.note: broken says the letters of end are scrambled

explanation.surface: An employer recruiting despite a fractured conclusion, getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking on' reads as accepting a task, but it means employing staff; 'broken' scrambles the end, and the result sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting in someone's way or impeding them is putting a block in their path.

clue.text: It gets blanket coverage in some paper

definitions.meaning: a bed covering of cloth lies under the blanket

explanation.surface: A newspaper giving something extensive coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed linen layer lies beneath the blanket, and a single leaf of paper has the same name.

clue.text: Conference in French city set up on a river

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the city's name is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Nimes is a city in southern France

explanation.surface: A meeting in a French city held beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses NIMES to SEMIN; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A group meeting for discussion, especially an academic class, is a kind of conference.

clue.text: Conclusions of board you dismissed as faulty

indicators.note: conclusions are the endings, so take the final letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: The board waved away your idea as defective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless or not working, like a shell that fails to explode, is called this.

clue.text: Combination of heat and cold ruined new Olympic event

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of heat and cold are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Athletes suffer through heat and cold that spoil a fresh Olympic contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination of' and 'and' join the two fodder words before 'ruined' scrambles them.
explanation.definitionFit: This ten-part track and field contest for men is a fixture of the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Unhappy with an empty broadcast, the first instalment

parts.note: down means low in spirits

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of an empty are spread and reformed

explanation.surface: Feeling gloomy about a vacant broadcast, the opening episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' sounds like a programme but here scatters AN EMPTY.
explanation.definitionFit: The initial lump sum paid when buying on credit is the opening part of the money owed.

clue.text: Ill-fated vessel in French tributary of Rhone

parts.note: the French word for in is en
the Durance is a river of southern France flowing into the Rhone

explanation.surface: A doomed ship found sailing on a French river that feeds the Rhone.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessel is Shackleton's Antarctic ship, crushed by pack ice in 1915.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackleton's expedition ship bore this name and was lost in the Weddell Sea ice.

clue.text: Parrot mimicking, initially, a call of another bird

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of mimicking

parts.note: caw is the cry of a crow or rook

explanation.surface: A parrot copying the cry of a crow.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly coloured tropical American parrot species goes by this name.

clue.text: Put forward nothing on page in plain language

indicators.note: in says the next pieces sit inside the word for plain language

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing, as opposed to verse
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone suggests writing nothing fancy on a page, just plain words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the zero before the page letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a motion or idea is to suggest it for consideration.

clue.text: Good person taking nation's part, in a way

indicators.note: in a way here means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A virtuous figure siding with the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link; the possessive mark adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is a holy, good person, and this one protects a place or a group.

clue.text: Young woman might appear in this turret?

definitions.text: Young woman might appear in this
definitions.meaning: a sleeveless knitted pullover a girl might wear
the top of a tank, its gun turret, read literally

explanation.surface: A girl popping up in the hatch of an armoured vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment's name, read as two words, also describes the upper part of a military tank.

clue.text: Pasta cut and rearranged for appetisers

indicators.note: the word pasta is chopped up and reordered into new letters

explanation.surface: Chopped and reworked pasta served as starters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small Spanish savoury dishes served with drinks are eaten as starters or snacks.

clue.text: Claim head is holding drink up

indicators.note: is holding says the head word contains the next piece

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the drink is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that a head is keeping a drink raised.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the drink from bottom to top; it then sits just after the head's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate something is to assert or affirm it as true.

clue.text: In a bad way, I am needing doctor to recover

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly says they need a doctor to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wickedly or without morals is behaving badly in the ethical sense.

clue.text: Spanish woman hiding Spanish man's drug

indicators.note: hiding says the woman's name conceals the man's name within it

parts.note: Maria is a common Spanish woman's name
Juan is a common Spanish man's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman conceals a Spanish man's narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis in its smoked form is a widely used recreational narcotic.

clue.text: Done like some small oysters, consumed with enthusiasm

parts.note: over means done or finished
eager describes someone full of keenness

explanation.surface: Little oysters, cooked and eaten with great relish.
explanation.walkthrough: The small oysters are the young ones in Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter, who hurried up all eager for the treat and were eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's poem the young oysters rush keenly to the feast and pay for that excess keenness.

clue.text: Take advantage of heroic achievement

definitions.meaning: to use something or someone for one's own benefit

explanation.surface: Someone cashing in on a brave feat.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means use for gain; as a noun it means a bold, daring deed.

clue.text: Accommodation some clergyman selected?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Housing given to a particular chosen minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's house, especially in Scotland, is the lodging provided by the church.

clue.text: Be included in special match that's not mentioned by players

indicators.note: included in says be is placed inside the rearranged letters
special signals the letters of match are reworked

explanation.surface: Being part of a special fixture the athletes refuse to talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' are actors, not sportsmen: theatrical superstition forbids naming Shakespeare's Scottish play in a theatre. 'special' turns MATCH into MACTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors call this tragedy the Scottish play, since naming it aloud backstage is thought unlucky.

clue.text: Was critical about power getting cut off

indicators.note: about says the critical word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: sniped means made sly critical remarks
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone complained bitterly after the electricity was disconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped with scissors means trimmed or severed.

clue.text: Copy as cheat, inserting aforementioned article ahead of time

indicators.note: inserting says the cheat word takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them

indicators.note: ahead of puts the article before the time letter

parts.note: it is the pronoun for the thing already mentioned

explanation.surface: A forger copies like a fraud, putting a prior item before the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the same again, used to repeat what was said above, so a duplicate.

clue.text: Sailor joining vessel gets big prize

indicators.note: joining says the sailor's name is followed directly by the vessel

parts.note: Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor
a pot is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A seaman linking up with a ship wins a big reward.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest prize in a lottery or game is often called this.

clue.text: Source of poetry in 17th century or earlier

definitions.meaning: Matthew ..., an English poet born in the 17th century

explanation.surface: A poetic origin from the 1600s or before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of poetry' tempts you to take the first letter of poetry; it is a poet. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means previous, and it was also the surname of the poet Matthew, who wrote from the 1680s.

clue.text: For example, monarch ultimately is villain, grabbing maiden

indicators.note: grabbing says the villain holds the maiden inside him

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Shakespeare's Othello
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A king turns out at last to be a scoundrel seizing a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarch' is not a king but the butterfly, which ultimately becomes an adult insect. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult, final stage of an insect such as a butterfly is its fully developed form.

clue.text: Essays about old dramatic works

indicators.note: about says the essays word goes around the next piece

parts.note: essays as a verb means attempts, tries
aged means old

explanation.surface: Critical essays written about classic plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essays' looks like written pieces but is the verb meaning attempts.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious plays ending in disaster, such as Hamlet, are works of this dramatic genre.

clue.text: Positive response from Italian reported in Rome, notably

indicators.note: reported says the Italian word is heard rather than read

parts.note: si is Italian for yes

explanation.surface: An Italian says yes, as heard in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Holy See, the Pope's bishopric, is in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's seat or diocese, the most famous being the Holy See at the Vatican.

clue.text: Starts from two or eight as digit

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, taken from each of the three words

explanation.surface: Counting from two or eight as a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digit' suggests a number but means a finger or toe; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any finger or the corresponding member of the foot.

clue.text: Present ploy that finally yielded dividends in long-term investment

definitions.text: Present ploy that finally yielded dividends in long-term investment

parts.words: Present ploy that finally yielded dividends in long-term investment
parts.note: the Greeks' wooden gift ended their ten-year siege of Troy; investment is also military besieging

explanation.surface: A gift scheme that eventually paid off for a patient investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is the old sense of besieging a city, so the long-term investment is the ten-year siege of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks' wooden gift hid soldiers inside and won the war, a trick disguised as a present.
